stem.text: Ethane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_3$, and fluoromethane, $\text{CH}_3\text{F}$, have the same number of electrons in their molecules.
What is responsible for this difference in boiling points?

B.text: $\text{CH}_3\text{F}$ has a permanent dipole, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_3$ does not.

C.text: $\text{CH}_3\text{F}$ has a strong C–F bond, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_3$ does not.

D.text: Hydrogen bonding occurs in $\text{CH}_3\text{F}$, but not in $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_3$.
